answer.evidence: radon/raw.py:72-79 `_find(tokens, token, value)` iterates `enumerate(reversed(tokens))` and compares `(token, value) == token_values[:2]`. On the first hit, which is the rightmost match, it returns `len(tokens) - index - 1`, mapping the reversed index back to the original index. If nothing matches, it raises `ValueError('(token, value) pair not found')` at line 79. Review points: (1) `reversed()` needs a sequence, so a generator passed in would raise TypeError; callers must pass a list. (2) Each token is sliced with `[:2]`, which allocates a tuple per iteration, and a direct comparison would avoid that. (3) Check that callers handle or intentionally propagate the ValueError. (4) Add tests for an empty list, a single match, duplicate matches (the last index must win), and a missing pair. The neighboring `_split_tokens` (lines 82-93) uses the same comparison but splits on every match. I spent little time on the other candidates, since a grep found no other reverse-search or last-occurrence logic in radon/complexity.py, radon/metrics.py or radon/visitors.py.
